competitorFacts.text: ARC Prize named Tufa Labs and its Duck agent the first-place open-source solution for the June 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 1 prize.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — Duck Harness technical overview
competitorFacts.text: Tufa Labs says its public Duck harness lets an LLM inspect game grids as image and text, write Python in a REPL, and keep context short by evicting older messages. This describes the published Milestone 1 system, not an unverified current submission.
Tufa Labs lists Dries Smit, Isaiah Pressman and Jeroen Cottaar among its AI researchers, with research interests spanning reinforcement learning, self-play and Bayesian methods.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — October 9 public competition post
competitorFacts.text: On October 9, 2026, Tufa Labs described a temporary setback in a public X post and said it remained dedicated to crushing competitors with overwhelming resources and compute.
Yi-Chia Chen’s Kaggle profile lists her as a Competitions Master and a double-degree student at National Taiwan University and Waseda University.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Yi-Chia Chen — Eedi third-place solution write-up
competitorFacts.text: Yi-Chia Chen authored a Kaggle write-up for a third-place solution in Eedi — Mining Misconceptions in Mathematics.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Yi-Chia Chen — public Kaggle profile and avatar
competitorFacts.text: Yi-Chia Chen’s public Kaggle account is threerabbits. The profile lists she/her pronouns and displays an avatar of two rabbits.
The ARChitects’ own 2025 solution write-up credits Jan Disselhoff under the Kaggle handle insanitycheck, alongside David Hartmann (dvhrtm) and Daniel Franzen (dfranzen).
The team’s 2025 technical report lists Jan Disselhoff at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.
NVIDIA’s December 2025 report identifies Ivan Sorokin and Jean-Francois Puget as NVIDIA researchers who competed as NVARC in the 2025 ARC Prize.
The 2025 NVARC team write-up credits sorokin and cpmpml. Both handles appear in the observed roster of the distinct 2026 NVARC3 entry. This does not establish an affiliation for every current member.

NVIDIA describes the separate 2025 NVARC ARC-AGI-2 solution as using synthetic data generation, test-time training and a fine-tuned 4B model. This is historical background, not a claim about the 2026 NVARC3 agent.
Jean-François Puget’s public GitHub profile identifies him as CPMP and links directly to the Kaggle account cpmpml.
NVIDIA’s author biography describes Jean-Francois Puget as a director and individual contributor whose team advances agentic AI and showcases NVIDIA tools and expertise in Kaggle competitions.
The rostered lukasaichberger Kaggle profile identifies its owner as Lukas Aichberger and links to his research website.
Johannes Kepler University Linz lists Lukas Aichberger at its Institute for Machine Learning and credits him on research about reasoning models and uncertainty evaluation.
Another rostered account, fses91, describes itself on Kaggle only as Florian; the public profile does not establish a surname.
The rostered dwellement0baser Kaggle profile identifies its owner as Mykyta Ielanskyi.

Johannes Kepler University Linz lists Mykyta Ielanskyi at its Institute for Machine Learning. Its research record credits him and Lukas Aichberger together on a 2026 paper about reward redistribution for reasoning models.
The ARChitects’ own 2025 solution write-up credits David Hartmann under the Kaggle handle dvhrtm, alongside Jan Disselhoff (insanitycheck) and Daniel Franzen (dfranzen).
The team’s 2025 technical report lists David Hartmann at Lambda, Inc.
The rostered richardcsaky Kaggle profile displays the name Richard Csaky.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Artificial Agency Lab — research and ARC-AGI-3 project
competitorFacts.text: Artificial Agency Lab says it built an ARC-AGI-3 agent combining structured grids and image observations with persistent context updates, keeping model weights fixed; it reports an eighth-place June milestone result.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Manifund — Artificial Agency ARC-AGI-3 project proposal
competitorFacts.text: A public ARC-AGI-3 project proposal names Richard Csaky as research lead and Côme Chevalier for engineering. The proposal describes an intended curiosity-driven proof of concept, not a verified method of the current Kaggle submission.
Richard Csaky’s Kaggle account published an “ARC-AGI-3 milestone 2 submission” notebook.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Artificial Agency Lab — own research and account links
competitorFacts.text: Artificial Agency Lab’s own site links Richard Csaky to @ricsinaruto and its September 30 ARC-AGI-3 submission; its dated historical methods do not identify the method behind the October 14 score event.
The sole rostered michaeltgao Kaggle account displays the public name Michael; the profile does not establish a surname.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Mostik — dated public launch and early-lead claim
competitorFacts.text: Mostik’s September 2, 2026 public launch post claimed first place on the ARC-AGI leaderboard; the post did not disclose the competition method.
The Kaggle account and team both use the public name Lord Han Solo. The profile itself does not supply a verified personal name.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Lord Han Solo — Milestone 2 Kaggle notebook
competitorFacts.text: Lord Han Solo published a Kaggle notebook titled “Built on Tufa Labs duck harness - Milestone 2,” explicitly crediting that earlier public harness in the notebook title.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: ARC Prize — Lord Han Solo official participant credit
competitorFacts.text: ARC Prize announced Lord Han Solo as second-place qualifying open-source ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 2 prize winner and directly linked the Kaggle profile lordhansolo.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize’s October 13 announcement reports DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at about 3% with its provider adapter and below 1% with the standard harness. The original linked verified-results table, refreshed October 14, gives a matched Low-reasoning comparison of 3.26% versus 0.35%; its headline best configurations differ in reasoning level. Organizer model evaluation, separate from Kaggle team submissions.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Public original read without sign-in in the in-app browser; linked primary results table independently read. Organizer evaluation, separate from Kaggle team standings.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Tufa Labs reclaimed first on the ARC-AGI-3 public Kaggle board with roughly 69%, up from roughly 56%. This is the author’s dated October 13 observation; refresh standings before publication.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Organizer confirmation of a consequential team result already covered in the newspaper’s morning/afternoon reporting; no methods disclosed.

socialPosts.author: OCEANVIN10
socialPosts.summary: OCEAN highlighted the Memento 3 preprint. Its authors report that a fixed language model revises an external rulebook and executable world model; on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, they report clearing every level with fewer actions than the human baseline. These are author-reported results on the public set.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A new ARC-AGI-3 research lead for the edition desk. The paper provides a concrete mechanism and results, but the public tutorial set cannot establish private-game performance.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced Yi-Chia Chen at 59.17% on the 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Kaggle board, taking the lead over Tufa Labs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Historical October 9 standings announcement, newly inventoried as a Chollet repost; not a fresh score move. Original and visible context re-read; existing independently verified public visibility preserved.

socialPosts.author: mhmazur
socialPosts.summary: Replying to Vlad Garbuz’s question about the provider checkpoint used for the DeepSeek evaluation, Mazur says Baseten serves the original DeepSeek V4.1 Flash checkpoint, which natively uses fp8 with mxfp4 experts, without additional quantization. Original reply and parent chain read in regular public-post UI, with no Subscribers restriction. This is Mazur’s testing clarification, not an independently reproduced provider comparison.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New organizer detail for interpreting the October 13 verified DeepSeek evaluation. Keep the native mixed precision distinct from additional provider quantization; no new Kaggle score or ruling.
